Dance/Electronic year-end #1 was 'Turn Down for What' (DJ Snake, France, with Atlanta's Lil Jon), listed as foreign by lead artist. New York: Brooklyn rapper Bobby Shmurda's 'Hot N*gga' (Shmoney dance; Hot 100 peak #6, year-end #54) was the city's breakout, and Romeo Santos is a Bronx act.

Puerto Rican artists are counted as home (US nationals). Five of the year-end top 13 were foreign (Mark Ronson and Ed Sheeran, UK; The Weeknd, Canada; OMI, Jamaica; Ellie Goulding, UK). The Weeknd is capped at two, so 'Can't Feel My Face' (#12) is left out. 'Lean On' is by the US-based group Major Lazer with DJ Snake (France) and MØ (Denmark), counted home by lead act. Christian year-end #1 not confirmed; Needtobreathe's 19 weeks at #1 is used. New York area: Fetty Wap of Paterson, New Jersey ('Trap Queen' #4, '679' #21, 'My Way' #44) had three songs on the year-end Hot 100; no Hot 97 or New York radio year-end list was found, so this rests on the national chart only.

Puerto Rican artists are counted as home (US nationals). Camila Cabello (Cuban-born, raised in Miami) is counted home. New York: Bronx rapper Cardi B's 'I Like It' with Bad Bunny and J Balvin (#7, built on a boogaloo sample) and Brooklyn rapper 6ix9ine's 'FEFE' (#31) on the year-end Hot 100.

Foreign acts (British, Canadian, Barbadian, Australian, Swedish, French and others) were a large share of US hits in this decade; foreign rows are the highest-placed non-American lead artists on the year-end Hot 100. Puerto Rican artists are counted as home (US nationals). An unusually American year at the top: the first foreign lead act on the year-end Hot 100 is at #14. 'Wow' (Post Malone, #5) and 'Sicko Mode' (Travis Scott, #9, a 2018 holdover) left out to make room for scene rows. 'Old Town Road' was the year-end #1 on both the Hot 100 and Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs and is a country-rap crossover. Christian year-end #1 not stated by the source; Lauren Daigle's 43 weeks at #1 is used. New York: Brooklyn drill breakout 'Welcome to the Party' by Pop Smoke was called the borough's and the city's summer anthem (Pitchfork, Complex) without a national year-end placing; Bronx rapper A Boogie wit da Hoodie's 'Look Back at It' was #41 on the year-end Hot 100.
